rationale: The head paradigm gives masxele/masxe. In this example masxewa is Infectum masxe plus -wa, rather than the Preterit masxele. The adjacent qoṭaʕwa likewise carries -wa. File this example in an Infectum-wa box in the same stem; retain the following example with lo masxele under Preterit.

rationale: The b-marked relative and prospective d məqṭəl express unwillingness to allow a person's death, distinct from spending property. One attestation; retain the lexical connection as a subsense.

rationale: First III.1b example; threat to the relative and the subject's armed intervention make the b-person/d-clause construction independently intelligible.

summary: The new b-person construction has a human bearer of risk and a d-clause specifying that person's prospective death. The subject resists the threatened event; no Detransitive reading of masxele is involved.
Regular III.1 covers reluctance to expend property and timber. Infectum-wa in the material-culture passage expresses former habitual reluctance, not a single completed act.
The headnote's Kurdish sexî kirin comparison is retained as inherited etymological information. The new Turoyo token is an inflected III verb, not itself an attestation of a light verb plus noun.
Negative polarity recurs in both passages, consistent with the inherited note normally used with negation. Two tokens do not establish an obligatory negative construction.
Confirm whether speakers group b-person plus d-clause in JTM 3.2/2 with reluctance to spend/sacrifice property, and whether III.1b is the right degree of separation.
Can the human-complement construction occur affirmatively, and what b-complement cases occur without a d-clause?
Confirm the expanded source identification for the old timber quotation; no change to its Turoyo spelling is proposed.
